source_lines_after.4: title: Structure of $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and root coordinates
source_lines_after.31: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $k$ be a field, $T_2$ the diagonal torus of $\mathrm{SL}_2$, $U^+=\{\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\}$ and $U^-=\{\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\a&1\end{pmatrix}\}$ ([[lem-general-linear-group-scheme-and-its-coordinate-ring]], [[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]). Then: (a) $\mathrm{SL}_2$ is generated by $U^+$ and $U^-$, and $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ are perfect; (b) the isomorphisms $u_\alpha(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $u_{-\alpha}(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\a&1\end{pmatrix}$ satisfy $tu_\alpha(a)t^{-1}=u_\alpha(\alpha(t)a)$ and $tu_{-\alpha}(a)t^{-1}=u_{-\alpha}(\alpha(t)^{-1}a)$ for $t=\operatorname{diag}(x,x^{-1})$ and the root $\alpha(t)=x^2$; (c) $n_\alpha=u_\alpha(1)u_{-\alpha}(-1)u_\alpha(1)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$ represents the nontrivial element $s_\alpha$ of $W(\mathrm{SL}_2,T_2)$, $n_\alpha^2=\alpha^\vee(-1)$, and $s_\alpha$ acts on $X(T_2)$ by $\chi\mapsto\chi-\langle\chi,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ with $\alpha^\vee=\operatorname{id}$; (d) the natural surjection $\mathrm{SL}_2\to\mathrm{PGL}_2$ is a central isogeny with kernel $\mu_2$, $\mathrm{SL}_2$ is simply connected, and every automorphism of $(\mathrm{SL}_2,T_2)$ maps $U^+$ to $U^+$ or $U^-$ and is determined by its restrictions to $T_2$ and $U^+$.
source_lines_after.52: 3.1 For (c), direct multiplication gives $u_\alpha(1)u_{-\alpha}(-1)u_\alpha(1)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}=n_\alpha$, and $n_\alpha^2=-I=\alpha^\vee(-1)$ where $\alpha^\vee:\mathbf G_m\to T_2$ is the cocharacter $t\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})$ with $\chi\circ\alpha^\vee=\operatorname{id}$. Since $n_\alpha\notin T_2$ but $n_\alpha$ normalizes $T_2$ (it conjugates $\operatorname{diag}(x,x^{-1})$ to $\operatorname{diag}(x^{-1},x)$), it represents the nontrivial element $s_\alpha$ of $W(\mathrm{SL}_2,T_2)$; the induced action on characters is $s_\alpha(\chi)=\chi-\langle\chi,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha=\chi-2\chi=-\chi$, the reflection in the root $\alpha=2\chi$. [F1, step 2.1, algebra]
